answer: Admission flows through a single rate-limited inlet that throttles registrations per fingerprint, making mass signups costly and slow. Each agent must stake a bond tied to a unique hardware kernel fingerprint, so spawning identities means buying new silicon, not just new keys. Any attempt to forge duplicate fingerprints triggers slashing of the full bond, so an attacker’s marginal cost per sybil rises with every fake identity.
